courses.title: Choose what you will build.
courses.lead: Engineer the chips, devices, robots and software behind AI. Or learn to take a product to market through BBA or MBA.

sections.title: Four ways to build AI systems

items.title: Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology)
items.text: Design a processor core and verify its logic. Suits students who enjoy precise work. Explore careers in chip design, verification and physical layout.

items.title: Electronics and Computer Engineering
items.text: Design circuit boards, write firmware and run AI on a device. Suits students who enjoy electronics and computing. Explore careers in firmware and product engineering.

items.title: Robotics and Artificial Intelligence
items.text: Program machines to sense and move. Suits students who want to see their code control a robot. Explore careers in robotics, automation and machine perception.

items.title: CSE (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning)
items.text: Train models, test predictions and build software. Suits students who enjoy maths and programming. Explore careers in applied AI, machine learning and data science.

sections.title: BBA and MBA
sections.intro: Work alongside engineers to bring a product to market. Learn how to finance it, source its parts and reach customers, using data and AI to guide decisions.
body: The four proposed specialisations apply to both degrees. Ask admissions which options are available at your preferred campus.

degrees.title: BBA
degrees.text: The Bachelor of Business Administration is an undergraduate route into business and management.

degrees.title: MBA
degrees.text: The Master of Business Administration is a postgraduate route into business and management.

items.title: AI for Business
items.text: Analyse business data and use AI to automate routine work and compare options.

items.title: Supply Chain and Operations Management
items.text: Plan how to source parts, manufacture products and deliver them to customers.

items.title: AI for Marketing and Sales
items.text: Use AI to identify customers, develop a brand and make sales decisions.

items.title: Entrepreneurship and New Ventures
items.text: Find customers, set a price and assess funding and growth options for a venture.

links.label: See BBA and MBA programme details

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: Projects get more demanding each semester and lead to a final term of supervised engineering work. Practical assessments record the skills each student can demonstrate independently.

courses/electronics-computer-engineering.title: Build the whole smart device.
courses/electronics-computer-engineering.lead: Design a circuit board, write its firmware and run an AI model on the device. Progress from a calibrated instrument to a pilot batch and a field trial.

sections.title: How a smart device works
body: A heart monitor or smartwatch turns a sensor reading into information someone can use. An EV charger measures and controls how power flows. All rely on circuits that collect signals and software that decides what to do with them.

sections.title: From calibrated instrument to field trial

items.title: Semester 1 · Smart measuring instrument
items.text: Design an instrument and calibrate its readings.

items.title: Semester 2 · Connected device
items.text: Build a working device on a circuit board you designed.

items.title: Semester 3 · Embedded signal processing
items.text: Build a board that can process a real-world signal.

items.title: Semester 4 · Real-time motor control
items.text: Build a controller that balances, steers or drives a motor.

items.title: Semester 5 · On-device AI
items.text: Run a model locally on a product powered by Linux.

items.title: Semester 6 · A 10-unit pilot batch
items.text: Build a secure product and produce its first 10 units.

items.title: Semester 7 · A field trial
items.text: Build a device that solves a user’s problem, then test it in the field.

items.title: Semester 8 · Engineering work
items.text: Spend 16–20 weeks working in a company or the Product Studio.

sections.title: Circuits, firmware and edge AI

items.title: Hardware
items.text: Design circuits and printed circuit boards. Work with ARM and RISC-V microcontrollers, FPGAs and design for manufacturing.

items.title: Software
items.text: Program in C, C++ and Python. Work with real-time operating systems, embedded Linux, device drivers and device security.

items.title: Embedded intelligence
items.text: Process signals, control hardware and run machine learning models on devices.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in embedded systems and firmware, edge AI, embedded Linux, IoT products, and automotive and EV electronics. The skills also support building a hardware startup.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The sequence introduces measurement and circuit design before embedded computing and control. Later projects test the device as a product through security checks, pilot manufacturing and a field trial. Individual practical assessments record what each student can demonstrate on their own.

links.label: See how projects and skill tests work

faq.question: What does Electronics and Computer Engineering cover?
faq.answer: You design the hardware, write the software that runs on it and learn to test them together.

faq.question: Does the degree prepare me for software roles?
faq.answer: The curriculum includes programming, data structures, operating systems and software engineering. These are foundations for software roles.

closing.title: See how a smart device comes together.
closing.text: Ask how the projects are assessed, from calibrating your first instrument to testing a device in the field.

courses/vlsi.eyebrow: B.Tech · Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology)
courses/vlsi.title: Design a chip from logic to layout.
courses/vlsi.lead: Test digital circuits on programmable hardware, design a processor core and learn to map a chip’s circuits onto silicon.

sections.title: Inside a silicon chip
body: A silicon chip can contain billions of transistors. Chip engineers design how those switches work together, verify the circuit and lay out the components on the chip. These skills support India’s investment in semiconductor manufacturing.

sections.title: From FPGA circuits to a chip layout
sections.intro: The proposed projects are shown by year. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

items.title: Year 1 · Digital circuits
items.text: Run and test the circuits you design on programmable FPGA boards.

items.title: Year 2 · Processor core
items.text: Design a core that fetches and executes instructions.

items.title: Year 3 · Circuit design and verification
items.text: Verify digital logic and work with analog and mixed-signal circuits.

items.title: Year 4 · Complete chip design
items.text: Take a chip from specification to physical layout, then spend a semester in supervised engineering work.

sections.title: Circuit design, verification and layout
body: The proposed curriculum starts with semiconductor devices and digital and analog circuits. Use Verilog and SystemVerilog for digital design and verification, then study computer architecture and physical design with industry tools.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in RTL design, design verification, physical design, analog and mixed-signal design, and semiconductor validation.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: An FPGA is a programmable chip. It lets you test a digital design on hardware while the design is still in development. Verification checks that the logic meets its specification, and physical design determines where to place and connect the components on silicon.

faq.question: What does VLSI stand for?
faq.answer: Very-large-scale integration. It is the design of complex circuits that integrate large numbers of transistors onto a single chip.

faq.question: Can I see the final list of projects?
faq.answer: Ask admissions for the current curriculum and project brief for the campus you are considering.

closing.title: Look inside the chip design course.
closing.text: Discuss the proposed FPGA and processor builds, and ask how the course progresses from testing logic to designing a chip layout.

courses/robotics-ai.title: Turn sensor data into controlled motion.
courses/robotics-ai.lead: Program a mobile robot to steer, control a robotic arm and use computer vision to guide a machine’s actions.

sections.title: How a robot acts on what it sees
body: A warehouse robot uses sensors to read its surroundings. Software interprets those readings, plans a path and adjusts the motors as the robot moves. The same process applies to robots working in farms, hospitals and factories.

sections.title: Mobile robots, arms and vision systems
sections.intro: The proposed projects are shown by year. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

items.title: Year 1 · Mobile robots
items.text: Use sensor readings to steer a robot you build.

items.title: Year 2 · Robotic arms
items.text: Build an arm and control its motion precisely.

items.title: Year 3 · Vision and navigation
items.text: Work on vision systems, drones and self-driving platforms.

items.title: Year 4 · Robot learning
items.text: Train a robot with data and simulation, then spend a semester in supervised engineering work.

sections.title: Motion control, perception and simulation
body: The proposed curriculum combines programming and algorithms with mechatronics, embedded systems and motor control. Study kinematics and motion planning, then work with computer vision, machine learning, ROS 2 and simulation.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in robotics, industrial automation, machine perception, autonomous systems and drone technology. The course also offers a foundation for building a robotics company.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The projects bring together sensor readings, perception and motion control. Simulation lets you test how a robot behaves before evaluating it on a physical machine. In team builds, each student demonstrates their practical skills individually.

links.label: See how projects and skill tests work

faq.question: How much of the course involves coding?
faq.answer: Programming and algorithms are core skills. You also write software for sensors, controllers, motion planning and machine vision.

faq.question: Do I need robotics experience to start?
faq.answer: The learning model starts with foundational skills and smaller builds. More complex projects follow as you practise programming, electronics and control.

closing.title: Explore the robotics project sequence.
closing.text: On your visit, ask how the proposed builds progress from a mobile robot to motion control, vision and simulation.

courses/cse-ai-ml.eyebrow: B.Tech · CSE (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning)
courses/cse-ai-ml.title: Train, test and deploy AI models.
courses/cse-ai-ml.lead: Prepare data, train models and test them on examples they’ve never seen. Build software for recommendation, computer vision and language.

sections.title: What makes a model reliable
body: A model learns patterns from its training data. Evaluate it on separate data to see how well it handles unfamiliar examples. Its errors show where you might need better data or a different model.

sections.title: From datasets to deployed software
sections.intro: The proposed projects are shown by year. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

items.title: Year 1 · Programs and data analysis
items.text: Write programs to analyse data and solve practical problems.

items.title: Year 2 · Machine learning models
items.text: Build and evaluate a model, such as a recommendation engine.

items.title: Year 3 · Vision and language applications
items.text: Develop software that uses computer vision, language models and generative AI.

items.title: Year 4 · An AI product for real users
items.text: Put an AI product in users’ hands, then spend a semester in supervised engineering work.

sections.title: Machine learning, data engineering and deployment
body: The proposed curriculum starts with Python, data structures, algorithms and mathematics for machine learning. It also covers deep learning, computer vision, language models and generative AI. Study how to prepare data, deploy and monitor models, and develop AI responsibly.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work as an AI or machine learning engineer, data scientist, applied AI engineer or MLOps engineer. The skills also support building an AI startup.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: MLOps covers what happens when a trained model goes into use. You deploy it, monitor how it performs and maintain it as the data or application changes.

links.label: See how AI is used in projects and assessments

faq.question: If AI writes code, why study computer science?
faq.answer: Computer science teaches you to design systems, evaluate the software a tool generates and improve the models that generate it.

faq.question: Will I learn to deploy a model?
faq.answer: The proposed curriculum includes model deployment and monitoring alongside training and evaluation.

closing.title: Follow a model from training to use.
closing.text: Ask an adviser how the proposed projects teach you to evaluate predictions and turn a model into working software.

courses/management.title: Take a product from lab to market.
courses/management.lead: Work with engineers to find customers, set a price and decide how to source, make and sell a product. Use data and AI to test those decisions against evidence.

summary.label: Focus
summary.value: Business decisions with data and AI

sections.title: From a prototype to a business
body: A working prototype raises new questions. Who will buy it? What will it cost to make and deliver? Engineers and managers answer those questions together as they prepare a product for the market.

sections.title: Two degrees, four specialisations
sections.intro: The BBA is proposed as a three- or four-year degree. The MBA is designed as a two-year degree. Confirm duration and specialisations for your preferred campus with admissions.

items.title: AI for Business
items.text: Analyse business data, automate routine work and use the findings to make decisions.

items.title: Supply Chain and Operations Management
items.text: Plan how to source, make and move products in India and internationally.

items.title: AI for Marketing and Sales
items.text: Use AI to find customers and support decisions about branding, marketing and sales.

items.title: Entrepreneurship and New Ventures
items.text: Find customers, set a price, explore funding and plan how a venture can grow.

sections.title: From first customer to factory order
body: Management students can join engineering teams to identify a first customer and prepare for a factory order. Company projects give students practice making business decisions within real constraints.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in business analysis, operations and supply chain, marketing and sales, or start a company of your own.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The programme applies business fundamentals to company projects and product work. Management and engineering teams use cost, customer and operations data to decide how to bring a product to market.

faq.question: Which degree should I explore?
faq.answer: The BBA is an undergraduate business degree. The MBA is a postgraduate business degree. Ask admissions which entry routes apply to you.

faq.question: Can BBA and MBA students choose the same specialisations?
faq.answer: The programme proposes the same four specialisations for both degrees. Confirm availability for your preferred campus with admissions.

closing.title: Find the right business programme for you.
closing.text: Compare the BBA and MBA routes with an adviser, and ask how each specialisation connects to company projects.
